title: 2023 Baulkham Hills Legal Studies Trial
notes: All 20 Section I answers are listed in the paper’s marking guidelines.

questions.stem: Which of the following offences does not require the prosecution to prove mens rea?

options.D: Selling alcohol to a person under the age of 18 years old

questions.answerNote: The paper’s Section I answer key lists D.

questions.stem: Between what ages for children can doli incapax be rebutted by the prosecution?
questions.answerNote: The paper’s Section I answer key lists B.

questions.stem:
Luna has been charged with being intoxicated in a public place.

What category of crime has Luna been charged with?
questions.answerNote: The paper’s Section I answer key lists C.

questions.stem:
Jamie is a suspect in a break-and-enter.

What are Jamie’s legal rights during detention and questioning?

options.A: Jamie’s right to bail and his right to cross-examination
options.B: Jamie’s right to a speedy trial and a right to a jury trial
options.C: Jamie’s right to a fair trial and right to cross-examination
options.D: Jamie’s right to remain silent and his right to legal representation

questions.answerNote: The paper’s Section I answer key lists A.

questions.stem:
The new nation-state of Westphalia decides not to sign The Covenant Against Torture and Other Cruel, Inhumane or Degrading Treatment of Punishment.

What is this an example of?

options.A: Complying with its international human rights obligations
options.C: Relying on the ICC to protect human rights

questions.answerNote: The paper’s Section I answer key lists D.

questions.stem:
After being abused for many years, Devona kills her partner while he is sleeping. Justice Lee directs a jury to find the defendant not guilty.

What can the jury do?

options.A: They must find the defendant guilty

questions.answerNote: The paper’s Section I answer key lists C.

questions.stem:
Penny pleads guilty and shows remorse for the charge of dangerous driving.

Which of the following best describes the key factor the magistrate will consider in sentencing her?

options.A: She lacked capacity, which is a mitigating factor
options.B: She was provoked, which is an aggravating factor
options.C: She had mens rea, which is an aggravating factor
options.D: She has saved the court’s time, which is a mitigating factor

questions.answerNote: The paper’s Section I answer key lists D.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the judicial arm of the United Nations?
questions.answerNote: The paper’s Section I answer key lists D.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true after a prisoner has served their minimum sentence?

options.A: He will be reclassified as a minimum-security prisoner
options.B: He can request another sentencing hearing

questions.answerNote: The paper’s Section I answer key lists C.

questions.stem: What are the legal requirements for issuing a search warrant?
questions.answerNote: The paper’s Section I answer key lists A.

questions.stem:
Supra has just moved into her new home. She is a little scared at night time, so she has placed a sticker on her front gate, “Beware of the dog”, even though she does not own a dog.

Which of the following is this an example of?
questions.answerNote: The paper’s Section I answer key lists C.

questions.stem:
Franco, a citizen of Sweden, commits a serious indictable offence while on holiday in NSW. He is sentenced to 5 years in prison.

What can the Australian government do once he completes his sentence?

options.A: Detain Franco indefinitely without a court order
options.B: Allow Franco to continue his holiday

questions.answerNote: The paper’s Section I answer key lists D.

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of the United Nations Human Rights Council?

options.A: Responsible for international peace and security
options.B: Responsible for resolving disputes by member states
options.C: Responsible for the promotion and protection of human rights
options.D: Responsible for representing member states at global forum discussions

questions.answerNote: The paper’s Section I answer key lists C.

questions.stem:
The Bail Amendment Act 2014 (NSW) introduced the ‘Show Cause Test’, which required an accused person to explain why they should not be held on remand.

Which principle of the rule of law did this bring into question?

options.D: The concept that no one is above the law

questions.answerNote: The paper’s Section I answer key lists A.

questions.stem:
Marleta is charged with murder. Her lawyer and the senior prosecutor discuss the facts of the case and the evidence.

This process is known as what?
questions.answerNote: The paper’s Section I answer key lists B.

questions.stem:
The island of Utopia has been given the power to govern themselves.

What is this concept known as?
questions.answerNote: The paper’s Section I answer key lists C.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of assigning a security classification to an offender when they are first placed in corrective services custody?

options.A: To classify the type of offence committed
options.B: To determine the offenders’ eligibility for parole
options.C: To determine the amount of time an offender will serve in custody
options.D: To determine the level of security needed for an offender placement in custody

questions.answerNote: The paper’s Section I answer key lists D.

questions.stem: Which of the following issues will breach the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights?

options.D: Banning media articles which criticise the government

questions.answerNote: The paper’s Section I answer key lists C.

questions.stem: Which TWO of the following are partial defences to murder?
questions.answerNote: The paper’s Section I answer key lists A.

questions.stem:
Mikaela works at a hotel. On Melbourne Cup Day, the hotel is expected to have many sales, with many customers paying with cash. Mikaela helps her brother plan a robbery at the hotel later that night. Mikaela is not with her brother when he commits the robbery.

What might Mikaela be charged with?
questions.answerNote: The paper’s Section I answer key lists A.
